# Ground-truth capture for the RFCOMM WiFi-bootstrap handshake.
#
# Captured 2026-09-18 via aa-proxy-rs's debug=true ProxyFrameSniffer,
# running in bt_wireless_proxy_mode="probe" on a Raspberry Pi against a
# real TF811BT motorcycle Android Auto display (Bluetooth MAC
# 00:88:21:0A:6C:0A, RFCOMM channel 4). Procedure: docs/capturing-ground-truth.md.
# aa-proxy-rs binary: ~/aa-project/aa-proxy-rs/target/release/aa-proxy-rs
# (built from https://github.com/aa-proxy/aa-proxy-rs, see that repo for
# the exact commit/version if needed).
#
# Two connection attempts are included (the probe reconnected once after
# the first RFCOMM session was reset by the peer at its 30s idle
# timeout) -- both produced an IDENTICAL frame sequence, which is good
# evidence this is stable/reproducible behavior, not a one-off fluke.
#
# Raw stdout from:
#   sudo timeout 45 aa-proxy-rs -c /etc/aa-proxy-rs/config.toml
# ANSI color codes stripped for readability; only the bluetooth-subsystem
# lines relevant to the RFCOMM bootstrap are included below (the full log
# also has unrelated USB-gadget-subsystem error lines interleaved between
# the two connection attempts -- this Pi has no USB gadget hardware
# configured, unrelated to Bluetooth/WiFi and not reproduced here).
#
# Decoded findings from this capture are written up in
# docs/protocol-notes.md and src/aa_hmi/messages.py's module docstring.
